title: Minimum Effective Dose
hook: That deck was done three hours ago. You just kept polishing it.
statement: Do just enough to hit the result you need, then stop.
explainer: Past a certain point, more effort buys tiny improvements at full price. Spotting where that curve bends protects your time for the stuff that actually moves things.
sop: Define what good enough looks like before you start.
Start with the simplest version that could hit it.
Score the Result against the target and the Effort it took, 1 to 10.
Stop as soon as it clears the bar.
Write down what the minimum was for next time.
equation_example: Result 8, Effort 4. 8 ÷ 4 = 2.0. Push that ratio as high as you can. Higher means a strong result on the cheap. Near or below 1 means you're putting in more than it's worth.
question: Name one thing you're overdoing where good enough would get you the same result.
closing_statement: The last 20% of polish rarely earns its cost.
caption:
Principle Nº 215: Minimum Effective Dose
